abstraction_fitness.issue_character: The main abstraction fitness problems are a pass-through wrapper in the Shell implementation (calculate_vfe adds no value over calculate_kl_divergence) and a leaky domain boundary in Python where visualization is inlined into the POMDP model class rather than separated.
abstraction_fitness.score_rationale: The stronger language implementations (TypeScript, Rust, Go) demonstrate earned abstractions with clear leverage. The Shell implementation has a concrete pass-through abstraction defect in calculate_vfe. The Python class conflates domain model and visualization in a single class, creating a leaky abstraction boundary. These issues are moderate — they impose real but navigable cost on a developer — consistent with the 70-80 anchor range. The absence of util dumping grounds and delegation-heavy classes keeps the score from falling lower.

issues.summary: calculate_vfe is a zero-value pass-through wrapper around calculate_kl_divergence
evidence: Lines 70-77: calculate_vfe calls calculate_kl_divergence with the same two arguments and immediately echoes the result with no transformation
The wrapper adds one level of function call overhead and a misleading name without introducing any new behavior, policy, or semantic
issues.suggestion: Remove calculate_vfe and call calculate_kl_divergence directly at the call site in run_simulation (line 208), or expand calculate_vfe to compute the full VFE formula (KL term + log-likelihood term) so the abstraction earns its existence

issues.summary: StudentTeacherPOMDP mixes domain model logic with matplotlib visualization, leaking view concerns into the model abstraction
evidence: Lines 95-156: plot_matrices, plot_student_beliefs, plot_teacher_knowledge are methods on StudentTeacherPOMDP — the domain POMDP class has a direct dependency on matplotlib

The class has two distinct responsibility clusters: probabilistic inference (update_beliefs, step, calculate_free_energy, infer_policy) and visualization (plot_*) — callers that want inference without visualization still carry the plotting dependency
issues.suggestion: Extract the three plot_* methods into a separate StudentTeacherVisualizer class or module that accepts a StudentTeacherPOMDP instance; the POMDP class should expose only its data (beliefs, matrices) and let the visualizer read them

issues.summary: infer_policy accepts a `policies` parameter that is never read, creating a false abstraction surface
evidence: Line 86: def infer_policy(self, policies): — the policies argument is declared
Lines 87-93: the function body uses only self.n_actions via range(); the policies parameter is never referenced
issues.suggestion: Remove the unused `policies` parameter from infer_policy's signature; callers in the __main__ block (line 177) pass random arrays that have no effect — removing the parameter makes the interface honest

root_causes: Shell implementation was likely scaffolded with placeholder wrapper functions that were never filled in
Python class grew organically — visualization was added directly to the model class for convenience during development and was not refactored out
likely_symptoms: AF-01 is a symptom of the same incomplete implementation root cause as NQ-01 in the naming batch
possible_false_positives: AF-02 could be considered acceptable for an educational/demo script where colocation of model and visualization simplifies the entry point
